notes: Lesson on cell theory and organelles. Structure: hook (cork microscopy history) → cell theory statement → prokaryotic vs eukaryotic comparison → plant vs animal cell diagram → key organelles × 6 with function descriptions → video → practice. Image-rich lesson.

units.label: Title: Cell Structure and Function
units.content_summary: Lesson title

units.label: Hook: Robert Hooke and cork microscopy (text + image)
units.content_summary: Robert Hooke (1665) observed cork under microscope and named the compartments 'cells' because they resembled monk's cells. Historical context establishing the discovery of cells.

units.label: Hooke's original cork microscopy drawing (image)
units.content_summary: Reproduction of Hooke's original drawing of cork cells from Micrographia (1665). Shows grid-like structure of dead cork cells.

units.label: Cell Theory: 3 principles (text)
units.content_summary: The Cell Theory: (1) all living things are made of cells; (2) the cell is the basic unit of life; (3) all cells come from existing cells. Credited to Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Objectives: state cell theory; compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; identify key organelles and their functions; distinguish plant and animal cells.

units.label: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic comparison diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Side-by-side diagram: prokaryotic cell (no nucleus, single circular chromosome, no membrane-bound organelles, example: bacteria) vs eukaryotic cell (true nucleus, complex organelles, example: animal/plant cells).

units.label: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic explanation (text)
units.content_summary: Defines prokaryotic (pro=before, karyon=nucleus) and eukaryotic (eu=true, karyon=nucleus). Describes key differences: nuclear membrane, organelles, size, complexity. Gives examples of each type.

units.label: Plant cell diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Labeled diagram of a plant cell showing: cell wall, cell membrane, nucleus, chloroplast, mitochondria, vacuole, endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes. Color-coded for clarity.

units.label: Animal cell diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Labeled diagram of an animal cell showing: cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, centrioles. Notably absent: cell wall, chloroplasts, large central vacuole.

units.label: Organelle 1: Nucleus function (text)
units.content_summary: The nucleus is the control center of the cell. Contains DNA (genetic information). Surrounded by nuclear envelope with pores. Nucleolus inside makes ribosomes. Found in all eukaryotic cells.

units.label: Organelle 2: Mitochondria function (text)
units.content_summary: Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell. Perform cellular respiration converting glucose + oxygen → ATP energy. Double-membrane structure. More numerous in cells with high energy demands.

units.label: Organelle 3: Chloroplast function (text)
units.content_summary: Chloroplasts perform photosynthesis: light + CO2 + water → glucose + oxygen. Contain chlorophyll (green pigment). Found only in plant cells and algae. Double membrane with thylakoid stacks.

units.label: Organelle 4: Cell membrane function (text)
units.content_summary: The cell membrane is the selective barrier controlling what enters and exits the cell. Composed of phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. All cells have a cell membrane.

units.label: Organelle 5: Cell wall function (text)
units.content_summary: The cell wall provides rigid structural support. Made of cellulose in plants, chitin in fungi, peptidoglycan in bacteria. Found in plant, fungal, and bacterial cells — NOT in animal cells.

units.label: Organelle 6: Vacuole function (text)
units.content_summary: Vacuoles store water, nutrients, waste products. Plant cells have one large central vacuole maintaining turgor pressure. Animal cells have small, temporary vacuoles. Important for plant structure.

units.label: Video: cell organelles tour (video)
units.content_summary: Animated 3-minute tour of an animal cell showing each organelle in context, describing its structure and function. Transitions between organelles with smooth animation.

units.label: Plant vs Animal cell: key differences table (image)
units.content_summary: Comparison table: structures present in plant cells (cell wall, chloroplasts, large central vacuole) vs those absent in animal cells. Three-column format: Structure | Plant Cell | Animal Cell.

units.label: Practice: organelle function matching (text)
units.content_summary: Six matching questions: match each organelle to its function. Covers nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplast, cell membrane, cell wall, vacuole.

units.label: Practice: plant vs animal cell identification (image)
units.content_summary: Two unlabeled cell diagrams. Students identify which is plant and which is animal based on presence/absence of key structures, and label 4 organelles in each.
